title: What If a Wave Taller Than the Empire State Building Hit?

scenes.text: What if a wave taller than the Empire State Building hit land? It already has, in Alaska.
In 1958, an earthquake shook a mountainside above Lituya Bay. About ninety million tons of rock dropped into the water.
The splash climbed five hundred twenty-four meters up the opposite ridge, one of the tallest tsunami waves ever recorded.
It sheared away about four square kilometers of forest. The scar was still visible from space more than sixty years later.
A fisherman's boat was lofted over a forested spit on the crest of the wave, and he lived to tell it.
Only two people died, because almost nobody was there. The same wave in a busy bay would be a very different story.

description:
What if a wave taller than the Empire State Building hit land?
In 1958 a rockslide in Lituya Bay, Alaska sent water 524 meters up a mountainside, the tallest tsunami wave on record.
What should we run through next?
